subject: Biology

stem: Which adaptation reduces drag caused by the viscosity of water when a seal swims?
solution: Streamlining reduces resistance as water flows around the body.

stem: In the Hershey-Chase experiment, radioactive phosphorus entered bacteria because it labelled what?
solution: DNA contains phosphorus in its phosphate backbone, whereas protein was labelled with sulfur.

stem: Which molecule has a phosphate-containing hydrophilic region and two hydrocarbon tails?
solution: This amphipathic structure allows bilayer formation.

stem: Which molecule crosses a membrane mainly through a channel protein?
solution: Charged ions require hydrophilic protein channels.

stem: Why does most enzyme activity fall at pH values far from the optimum?

options.html: Ionization changes disrupt active-site shape and bonding
All peptide bonds are immediately hydrolysed

solution: Changes in charge disrupt tertiary interactions and substrate binding.

stem: In a respirometer, carbon dioxide is absorbed. What does movement of the manometer fluid measure?
solution: With CO2 removed, gas-volume decrease reflects oxygen consumption.

stem: Which event occurs in the Krebs cycle?

options.html: Oxygen is split to release electrons
Glucose is phosphorylated in the cytoplasm
Carbon dioxide is released while NAD is reduced

solution: Decarboxylation and dehydrogenation occur in the cycle.

stem: What is produced directly by the light-dependent reactions?
solution: Photophosphorylation and photolysis supply ATP, NADPH and O2.

stem: Why do shorter DNA fragments move farther during gel electrophoresis?

options.html: They pass more easily through pores in the gel
They carry a more positive charge
They contain more phosphate groups per base
They are attracted to the negative electrode

solution: The gel matrix retards larger fragments more strongly.

stem: Which change can occur because the genetic code is degenerate?

options.html: One codon specifies several amino acids
Different codons specify the same amino acid
Stop codons code for rare amino acids

solution: Degeneracy means redundancy in codon assignment.

stem: Two DNA coding sequences differ by one base but encode the same polypeptide. What best explains this?

options.html: A stop codon replaced the start codon

solution: Degeneracy can make a base substitution silent.

stem: Which statement describes viruses outside host cells?
solution: Viruses require host machinery for replication and metabolism.

stem: A micrograph shows stacked flattened cisternae with budding vesicles. Which organelle is shown?
solution: The Golgi modifies and sorts products in stacked cisternae.

stem: Which protein performs primary active transport?
solution: The pump hydrolyses ATP to move ions against their gradients.

stem: Which channel is opened directly by neurotransmitter binding?

options.html: A leak channel controlled by ATP

solution: The ligand acts as the gating signal.

stem: What is a function of a lysosome?
solution: Lysosomes digest macromolecules and worn organelles.

stem: Which example demonstrates quorum sensing?

options.html: Bacteria emit light only after an autoinducer reaches a threshold
A neuron fires after reaching threshold voltage

solution: Quorum sensing coordinates bacterial gene expression according to population density.

stem: Which part of a multipolar neuron receives most synaptic inputs?
solution: Dendrites branch extensively and bear many synapses.

stem: During plant-cell mitosis, sister chromatids are moving toward opposite poles. Which stage is shown?
solution: Centromeres divide and chromatids separate during anaphase.

stem: A plant cell has pressure potential +0.50 MPa and solute potential -0.82 MPa. What is its water potential?
solution: Water potential equals pressure potential plus solute potential.

stem: Which pair belongs to the same genus?
solution: The first word of a binomial is the genus.

stem: Which set of organisms forms a clade?

options.html: Any organisms sharing one analogous trait
An ancestor and all of its descendants
All organisms at the same trophic level
Two species with the same common name

solution: A clade is monophyletic.

stem: A lower pH shifts the oxygen dissociation curve to the right. What is the consequence?

options.html: Haemoglobin binds oxygen more strongly at all pressures
Red blood cells stop producing ATP
Haemoglobin releases oxygen more readily to active tissues

solution: The Bohr effect supports oxygen unloading where CO2 and H+ are high.

stem: Which vessel has a thick muscular wall and relatively small lumen?
solution: Arteries withstand and regulate high-pressure blood flow.

stem: How are sieve-tube elements adapted for translocation?

options.html: They have few organelles and connect through sieve plates
They have lignified walls and no companion cells
They contain many nuclei and no cytoplasm

solution: Reduced contents lower resistance; companion cells support loading and metabolism.

stem: Which structure is the effector in a withdrawal reflex?
solution: The effector contracts to produce the response.

stem: A shoot bends toward unilateral light because what occurs?

options.html: Auxin destroys cells on the lit side
Cytokinin closes stomata on the shaded side
Auxin accumulates on the shaded side and promotes elongation
Ethylene accumulates equally on both sides

solution: Differential elongation curves the shoot toward light.

stem: What is a major role of helper T cells?

options.html: Secretion of cytokines that activate other lymphocytes

solution: Helper T cells coordinate adaptive immunity.

stem: Which sequence correctly describes oogenesis?

options.html: Mitotic proliferation, meiosis with arrests, unequal cytokinesis
Meiosis before any mitosis, then equal cytokinesis
Continuous meiosis producing four equal ova

solution: Oogenesis produces one large ovum and polar bodies through unequal divisions.

stem: An unaffected father and carrier mother have a daughter. What is the probability that the daughter is colour-blind for an X-linked recessive trait?
solution: Every daughter receives the father's normal X chromosome.

stem: A test cross AB/ab x ab/ab produces 44% AB, 43% ab, 7% Ab and 6% aB. What is the recombination frequency?
solution: Recombinants are Ab and aB: 7% + 6% = 13%.

stem: Why does skin blood flow increase during prolonged exercise in heat?

options.html: It lowers oxygen delivery to all tissues
It creates a positive feedback rise in temperature
It raises heat transfer from core to surface

solution: Vasodilation supports heat loss by radiation and convection.

stem: Which observation provides evidence for common ancestry?

options.html: Different vertebrate forelimbs share the same underlying bone pattern
Unrelated wings perform the same function

solution: Homologous structures reflect inheritance from a common ancestor.

stem: Which intervention best reduces extinction risk in fragmented populations?

options.html: Select one genotype for all releases
Restore corridors and maintain genetic exchange

solution: Connectivity reduces inbreeding and permits recolonization.

stem: What describes holozoic nutrition?

options.html: Absorbing dissolved organic matter without ingestion
Ingesting food and digesting it internally
Using inorganic chemicals as an energy source

solution: Holozoic organisms ingest particulate organic material.

stem: What do orchid mycorrhizal fungi commonly provide to germinating orchid seeds?
solution: Tiny orchid seeds depend on fungal partners for resources.

stem: In a food web, what does an arrow from crab to heron indicate?

options.html: Chemical energy passes from crab to heron
The crab preys on the heron
The heron provides carbon dioxide to the crab
Both occupy the same trophic level

solution: Food-web arrows point from resource to consumer.

stem: Which outcome is produced by directional selection?

options.html: The population mean shifts toward one phenotypic extreme

solution: Directional selection favours one extreme.

stem: The first lichens colonize new volcanic rock. What type of succession begins?
solution: Primary succession begins where soil and an established community are absent.

stem: Earlier flowering dates consistently follow warmer springs. What is this an example of?
solution: Phenology studies seasonal timing of biological events.
